model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The diagram is a nested pie chart comparing the distribution of various character categories. 
The chart consists of two layers, with the inner layer divided into three main sectors and the outer layer further subdividing one of these sectors into additional categories. 
The inner layer has three sectors: "Custom Characters" in red, occupying a relatively small portion; "Real Characters" in green, also taking up a smaller share; and "Virtual Characters" in blue, making up the largest part. 
The outer layer, colored in different shades of blue and pink, represents subcategories under "Virtual Characters" and "Custom Characters" and further subdivides "Real Characters" into "Scientists", "Artists", "Athletes", "Writers", "Musicians", "Actors", and "Influencers" in various shades of green. 
The "Virtual Characters" sector is further divided into "Game Characters," "Novel Characters," "Movie Characters," and "Comic Characters," with "Game Characters" being the largest among these subcategories. 
The chart includes a total of 11 sectors across both layers. 
The diagram does not include explicit percentage labels or a legend, but the relative sizes of the sectors can be visually compared. 
The sectors appear to be arranged in a somewhat ordered manner, with the largest sectors generally positioned towards the top and the smaller ones towards the right and bottom. 
Overall, the chart provides a visual representation of how different character categories are distributed, with "Virtual Characters" being the dominant category.
model_annotations.English: The pie chart compares the distribution of various character categories, divided into two main groups: "Virtual Characters" and "Real Characters." The chart is divided into 11 slices. The largest slice, "Game Characters," is light blue and represents roughly one-quarter of the chart, while "Virtual Characters" is dark blue and encompasses nearly half of the chart. Other notable slices include "Novel Characters" and "Comic Characters," both shades of blue, and "Movie Characters," a lighter blue, which together with "Game Characters," "Novel Characters," and "Comic Characters" make up the majority of the "Virtual Characters" category. The "Real Characters" category is represented by a green slice and is further divided into smaller subcategories, including "Influencers," "Actors," "Musicians," "Writers," "Athletes," "Artists," and "Scientists," with "Influencers" and "Actors" being the largest subcategories. "Custom Characters" is represented by a red slice and is positioned between "Virtual Characters" and "Real Characters." The chart does not include a legend, and percentage labels are not shown inside the slices. The segments appear to be ordered in a way that groups related categories together, with the "Virtual Characters" category being the most prominent.
model_annotations.German: The chart is a nested pie chart that compares the distribution of characters across different categories. There are 11 segments in total, divided into two main categories: "Virtual Characters" and "Real Characters". The "Virtual Characters" category is further divided into 6 sub-segments, namely "Comic Characters", "Movie Characters", "TV Characters", "Novel Characters", "Game Characters", and "Custom Characters", which are colored in various shades of blue and account for approximately 75% of the chart. The "Real Characters" category is divided into 5 sub-segments, namely "Scientists", "Artists", "Athletes", "Writers", "Musicians", "Actors", and "Influencers", which are colored in different shades of green and pink and make up around 25% of the chart. The chart does not have a legend, but the segments are labeled with their respective names. The "Virtual Characters" category is larger than the "Real Characters" category, and within the "Virtual Characters" category, the sub-segments are arranged in a clockwise direction, starting from "Comic Characters".
